Framework callback, locking, and security claims are scoped to current official documentation.

evidence: Checked record tuple a=(k,v,p), command/context transition f, valid states A_v, rejection set R, guarded persistence w, affected-row cases, and multi-record transaction statement.
Checked version increment/substitution and conditional one/zero row semantics.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Source-level record transitions are separated from database transaction, constraint, authorization, and distributed-effect premises.

evidence: Checked I-7 first approval changes version 2->3 and status pending->approved.
Checked stale expected 2 versus row 3 produces no row change and restores local status pending.
Checked denied I-8 remains pending/version 1; reproduced exact three-line output.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The finite model has no money arithmetic, batching, real lock, or concurrent threads.

evidence: Derived successful transition from actor/state/version premises and monotone v'=v+1.
Checked stale branch returns before row replacement and restores the pre-attempt local status.
Checked denied branch returns before candidate mutation or save.

evidence: Reviewed row-local fit versus rich/cross-row rules, invalid lifecycle, null/range/unique/reference races, stale/missing rows, lock timeout/deadlock, rollback object state, nested transactions/savepoints, commit uncertainty, and idempotency.

Reviewed unscoped tenant lookup, guessed ID, role/action authority, mass/nested assignment, protected fields, dynamic SQL, over-disclosure, default scope, soft delete/reuse/legal hold, and record-level security.

Reviewed association cardinality/cascade/order, N+1/eager multiplication/pagination, callback recursion/order/bypass/precommit effects/after-commit loss, bulk/native version/event bypass, STI discriminator, generated fields, rolling migrations, privacy, and clinical result release.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real framework, database, workload, broker, security, migration, and clinical evidence remain outside the finite model.

evidence: Traced row-centered ownership, scoped parameterized lookup, domain-named methods, constraints, application transaction, expected versions, callback limits, association semantics, bulk governance, and real integration testing through exposition/examples/answers.

invariant_checking.notes: Active Record convenience is not presented as automatic atomicity, authorization, or domain correctness.

evidence: Reviewed first approval, stale approval, denied approval, and limitation premises line by line.

Reviewed counterexamples for uniqueness validation race, per-save partial operation, external callback effect, after-commit loss, untrusted expected version, mass assignment, default-scope security, N+1/eager joins, bulk bypass, and hidden clinical callback.

evidence: Audited atomic, transaction, committed, validated, constrained, authorized, idempotent, callback, delivered, safe, conflict, proof, and conclusion language.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter distinguishes Active Record from Data Mapper, row/table gateways, Transaction Script, Table Module, Domain Model, projections, Service Layer, Unit of Work, and workflow without denigrating or universalizing the pattern.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
